stills.file: Photo composite of suspected water plumes on Europa.jpg
stills.author: NASA, ESA, W. Sparks (STScI), and the USGS Astrogeology Science Center
stills.description: This composite image shows suspected plumes of water vapor erupting at the 7 o'clock position off the limb of Jupiter's moon Europa. The plumes, photographed by Hubble’s Imaging Spectrograph, were seen in silhouette as the moon passed in front of Jupiter. Hubble's ultraviolet sensitivity allowed for the features, rising over 160 kilometres above Europa's icy surface, to be discerned. The water is believed to come from a subsurface ocean on Europa. stills.author: NASA/Noah Kroese, I.NK
stills.description: Scientists have found evidence of plate tectonics on Jupiter's moon Europa. This conceptual illustration of the subduction process (where one plate is forced under another) shows how a cold, brittle, outer portion of Europa's 20-30 kilometer-thick (roughly 10-20 mile) ice shell moved into the warmer shell interior and was ultimately subsumed. A low-relief subsumption band was created at the surface in the overriding plate, alongside which cryolavas may have erupted.

stills.description: Uploader's notes: The NASA-published closeup images have been converted from TIFF to JPEG format, the globe/location key has been cropped and enlarged, and the images combined by the uploader. Synopsis of original captions released with images: The surface of Jupiter's moon Europa features a widely varied landscape, including ridges, bands , small rounded domes and disrupted spaces that geologists called " chaos terrain ."
